title: 1953 AHSME Problem 1
statement: A boy buys oranges at \(3\) for \(10\) cents. He will sell them at \(5\) for \(20\) cents. In order to make a profit of \(\$1.00,\) he must sell:

solutions.text:
Each orange costs \(\frac{10}{3}\) cents and sells for \(4\) cents, so the profit is \(4-\frac{10}{3}=\frac{2}{3}\) cent per orange. To earn \(100\) cents, he must sell \[ \frac{100}{\frac{2}{3}}=150 \] oranges.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Find the buying cost and selling price per orange
The profit per orange is the difference of the two unit rates
